deed: גיל שוד ייסד את צ'ק פוינט — חברת אבטחת הסייבר הטהורה הגדולה בעולם
title: Gil Shwed, founder of Check Point

trailer.text: Check Point is the largest pure-play cybersecurity company in the world.
Shwed was selected to receive the Israel Prize for Lifetime Achievement in technology and applied innovation.

glance.label: Founders
glance.value: Gil Shwed, Shlomo Kramer and Marius Nacht

paragraphs.text: Gil Shwed was born in Jerusalem.
At age 10 he began taking computer classes once a week in his home town.
According to Shwed, at age 14, while still at school, he started working almost full-time as a system administrator at the Hebrew University.

stations.title: An idea born in the army

paragraphs.text: According to reports, Shwed served in the Intelligence Corps in Unit 8200, where he built military computer networks.
During his four years of service in the IDF, the idea for stateful inspection first came to him.
After the army, Shwed joined the Israeli company Optrotech as a software developer, where he met Marius Nacht.

stations.title: An apartment, three friends and 14 hours a day

paragraphs.text: In those days few people knew what the internet was, and even fewer knew that it created a security risk that needed guarding against.
Shwed said that when he first started out he had to persuade people that there was a market for the internet.
The three understood that businesses that connected to the internet would need safeguards, and so a market was created for blocking and protocol control capabilities.
In April 1993 the idea that later evolved into FireWall-1 was first developed.
In July 1993 the three founded Check Point.
Shwed, Kramer and Nacht worked for a year in a relative's apartment, programming 12 to 14 hours a day.
FireWall-1 was first presented to the public at the NetWorld Interop show in Las Vegas in 1994.
It won the best-in-show award, which helped bring Check Point into the limelight.
According to CIO, it was the first mass-market firewall.
Check Point's uniqueness was that it transferred the technology from UNIX systems to the PC environment.
In 1994 the company signed an OEM agreement with Sun Microsystems, and a year later a deal with HP.
The partnership with Sun turned Check Point from an insignificant company into a market leader.

stations.title: From a small company to a global market

paragraphs.text: Check Point went public in 1996.
Around the time Check Point was founded in 1993, about forty firewall companies sprang up, competing in the internet communications security market.
In the two years before 1999, Shwed had to face analysts' estimates that the firewall market was about to disappear.
According to Globes in 1999, Check Point undisputedly controlled the global market, its value exceeded $5 billion, and its name was a synonym for the entire sector.
According to the company, FireWall-1 is installed at every company on the Fortune 100 list.
Check Point also claims that it has never been breached.
The stateful inspection technology that Shwed developed and patented is still used by modern firewalls.
The company's products include firewalls, UTM appliances and endpoint security.
According to Check Point's annual report to the US Securities and Exchange Commission, the company owns its headquarters in Tel Aviv.
Calcalist wrote that Check Point is considered the largest Israeli company, following the decline in Teva's standing.
Shwed said that the company sees itself as a technology company, not a military or an Israeli company.
He said that he is proud of being Israeli but recognizes the limitations, because the American customer wants an American model.
According to CIO, he sees Check Point as a global company.
Shwed criticized the proliferation of startups and planning to set up a company in order to sell it, and said that a company is like a child.
He said that he likes what he does, and that the chances of founding another company as interesting and successful are not high.
According to him, information security is much more competitive today, and it is hard to develop something completely new in it.
Calcalist: since the company's founding
Shwed was selected to receive the Israel Prize for Lifetime Achievement in technology and applied innovation.
This is the first time the prize is awarded in this field, and the laureate was chosen by a committee headed by Shlomo Dovrat.
Education Minister Bennett initiated the new category in the Israel Prize to mark the celebrations of the State's 70th anniversary.
According to the prize committee, his contribution to developing the Israeli high-tech industry has continued for almost 25 years.
The committee noted the creation of thousands of jobs and the representation of Israel's excellence and human capital in the world.
Bennett wrote on Twitter that Shwed is the pioneer of the Start Up Nation, and that his story is the story of Israeli high-tech.
Shwed said that the prize belongs to all Check Point employees over the past 25 years.
According to Srugim, many see him as the father of the modern firewall.
In 2002 he appeared on Forbes' list of billionaire babies under 35, and as a result some wags in Israel called him the Bill Gates of Israel.
Globes named him "Person of the Year" in 2014.

stations.title: Beyond the company: youth and education

paragraphs.text: Shwed is a member of the board of trustees of Tel Aviv University, and he is chairman of the board of trustees of its Youth University.
The Israel Prize committee noted his public activity promoting leadership and excellence among gifted youth.
There are several different estimates of his personal wealth.
